KITCHEN & FOOD SERIES

🥗 16 Healthy Daily Recipes

Simple single-serve meals built on fresh ingredients, gentle cooking and everyday variety — with exact quantities, methods, allergens and chef’s notes.

Healthy Eating That Works Every Day

Guests today expect more from a menu than comfort and indulgence. They want dishes that taste good, look fresh and leave them feeling well, and they expect a hotel, restaurant or café to offer those dishes every day, not only on a special health page. A healthy daily menu does not need exotic ingredients or complicated techniques. It needs simple meals, balanced portions, sensible cooking methods and a team that understands why each dish works.

This guide collects sixteen healthy daily recipes, each written for a single serving so that kitchens can scale up for a full service or families can cook for one. They cover breakfasts, bowls, salads, a soup, a wrap, pasta and a dinner plate, and every one uses everyday ingredients: whole grains, pulses, vegetables, fruit, lean proteins and a small amount of olive oil. Each recipe gives the exact ingredients, a short method, the main allergens and a chef's note for safe, consistent service. The infographic poster at the bottom of the page summarises all sixteen on one sheet that you can download and display in your kitchen or training room.

What Makes a Recipe Healthy in a Professional Kitchen

Healthy cooking is a set of habits rather than a list of banned foods. The sixteen recipes here follow the same habits, and once a team understands them, they can be applied to almost any dish on the menu.

Start with vegetables. Nearly every recipe on this page includes spinach, broccoli, tomato, cucumber, pepper, carrot or mushrooms, often several of them. Vegetables add colour, fibre and volume, so the plate looks generous while the portion stays moderate.

Choose lean proteins and plant proteins. Chicken breast, white fish, eggs, tofu, Greek yogurt, lentils, chickpeas and kidney beans supply protein without heavy fat. Pulses are also inexpensive, which helps food cost, and they keep well in the store room.

Favour whole grains and slow energy. Rolled oats, quinoa, brown rice, whole-wheat pasta, whole-wheat couscous and whole-wheat tortillas keep guests fuller for longer than refined alternatives, and they bring a nutty flavour and pleasant texture.

Use fat with intention. The recipes call for a teaspoon or two of olive oil, a small handful of nuts or half an avocado. Fat carries flavour and helps the body absorb certain vitamins, so the aim is not to remove it but to measure it.

Season with flavour, not salt. Lemon and lime juice, fresh parsley, cumin, paprika, garlic, cinnamon and dried herbs do the work that heavy salt and sauces would normally do. Where soy sauce appears, the recipes specify a reduced-sodium version in small quantities.

Cook gently. Roasting, baking, grilling, simmering and quick stir-frying need very little oil and protect the natural flavour of the food. Deep frying does not appear anywhere in this collection.

BREAKFAST

1. Oatmeal Berry Bowl

Serves 1 • 10 min

A warm bowl of creamy oats simmered in low-fat milk and topped with berries, banana and chia. It is the simplest way to give a breakfast menu a wholesome option, because the oats release slow energy and the fruit adds natural sweetness without needing extra sugar.

Ingredients

  • 40 g rolled oats
  • 200 ml low-fat milk
  • 75 g mixed berries
  • ½ banana, sliced
  • 1 tsp chia seeds
  • 1 tsp honey (optional)

Method

  1. Simmer oats and milk for 5–7 minutes, stirring.
  2. Add fruit and chia. Drizzle with honey if desired.

Allergens: Milk, oats (gluten cross-contact), honey

Chef’s note: Stir constantly near the end to stop the base catching. Offer honey on the side so guests can control the sweetness.

BREAKFAST

2. Vegetable Omelette

Serves 1 • 15 min

A classic protein-rich breakfast made with spinach, tomato, bell pepper and onion folded into soft eggs. Cooked with only a teaspoon of oil, it shows that a hot egg dish can be light, colourful and filling at the same time.

Ingredients

  • 2 eggs
  • 30 g spinach
  • ½ small tomato, diced
  • ¼ bell pepper, diced
  • 2 tbsp chopped onion
  • 1 tsp olive oil
  • Black pepper, to taste

Method

  1. Sauté onion and pepper in oil. Add tomato and spinach.
  2. Pour in beaten eggs. Cook until fully set, then fold.

Allergens: Egg

Chef’s note: Cook the eggs until fully set, never runny, for guests in higher-risk groups. Keep egg-free pans separate for allergy orders.

LUNCH OR DINNER

3. Chicken Quinoa Bowl

Serves 1 • 25 min

Grilled chicken breast over fluffy quinoa with cucumber, tomato and lettuce, finished with olive oil and lemon. Quinoa is a complete grain-like seed with a pleasant bite, which makes this bowl a dependable high-protein option for lunch service and room dining.

Ingredients

  • 120 g raw chicken breast
  • 50 g dry quinoa
  • ¼ cucumber, diced
  • 1 small tomato, diced
  • 30 g lettuce
  • 1 tsp olive oil
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice

Method

  1. Cook quinoa according to the pack.
  2. Grill chicken until the centre reaches 74°C.
  3. Slice and serve with quinoa, vegetables, oil and lemon.

Allergens: None of the major allergens as written

Chef’s note: Probe the thickest part of the chicken and record 74°C. Rest the meat briefly before slicing so it stays juicy.

SOUP OR LIGHT DINNER

4. Lentil Vegetable Soup

Serves 1 • 30 min

Red lentils simmered with carrot, tomato and onion in low-sodium stock, with spinach stirred in at the end. Red lentils break down without soaking, so the soup turns thick and comforting with very little effort and very little fat.

Ingredients

  • 60 g dry red lentils, rinsed
  • 1 small carrot, diced
  • 1 small tomato, chopped
  • 30 g spinach
  • ¼ onion + 1 garlic clove, chopped
  • 350 ml low-sodium vegetable stock
  • 1 tsp olive oil

Method

  1. Sauté onion and garlic in oil.
  2. Add carrot, tomato, lentils and stock. Simmer 20–25 minutes until tender.
  3. Stir in spinach; cook for 2 minutes. Add water if needed.

Allergens: None of the major allergens as written

Chef’s note: Soups thicken as they stand, so loosen with hot water at service. Cool leftovers quickly and reheat until steaming hot.

DINNER

5. Baked Fish & Vegetables

Serves 1 • 30 min

A white fish fillet baked over roasted broccoli, carrot and bell pepper with lemon and dried herbs. Oven cooking needs almost no added fat, and a single tray gives guests lean protein and a full serving of vegetables in one dish.

Ingredients

  • 150 g white fish fillet
  • 80 g broccoli florets
  • 1 small carrot, thinly sliced
  • ½ bell pepper, sliced
  • 1 tsp olive oil
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • ½ tsp dried mixed herbs

Method

  1. Heat oven to 200°C. Toss vegetables with oil and roast for 10 minutes.
  2. Add fish, lemon and herbs. Bake 12–15 minutes, until fish flakes easily.

Allergens: Fish

Chef’s note: Fish is ready when it flakes easily and turns opaque. Declare fish clearly on the menu for allergy-aware guests.

LUNCH

6. Chickpea Avocado Salad

Serves 1 • 10 min

Chickpeas, avocado, cucumber, cherry tomatoes and parsley tossed with lemon juice and olive oil. It needs no cooking if you use cooked chickpeas, which makes it one of the fastest plates on the page and a dependable vegan choice.

Ingredients

  • 120 g cooked chickpeas, drained
  • ½ avocado, diced
  • ¼ cucumber, diced
  • 80 g cherry tomatoes, halved
  • 1 tbsp chopped parsley
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • 1 tsp olive oil

Method

  1. Combine chickpeas, avocado, cucumber, tomatoes and parsley.
  2. Toss gently with lemon juice and olive oil. Serve fresh.

Allergens: None of the major allergens as written

Chef’s note: Dice the avocado last and toss gently, since lemon juice slows browning but does not stop it. Serve the same day.

DINNER

7. Chicken Brown Rice Stir-Fry

Serves 1 • 20 min

Sliced chicken, broccoli, carrot and bell pepper stir-fried with garlic and served over brown rice, seasoned with a little reduced-sodium soy sauce. It is a quick, balanced plate that works well for banquets, staff meals and room service alike.

Ingredients

  • 120 g raw chicken breast, thinly sliced
  • 150 g cooked brown rice
  • 60 g broccoli, small florets
  • ½ carrot, thinly sliced
  • ¼ bell pepper, sliced
  • 1 garlic clove, minced
  • 1 tsp oil + 1 tsp reduced-sodium soy sauce

Method

  1. Heat oil; stir-fry chicken and garlic.
  2. Add vegetables and a splash of water. Cook until tender and chicken is fully cooked.
  3. Add rice and soy sauce; stir-fry until steaming hot.

Allergens: Soy (and usually wheat in soy sauce)

Chef’s note: Cool cooked rice quickly and refrigerate promptly if you pre-cook it, and reheat until steaming hot. Soy sauce normally contains wheat.

BREAKFAST OR SNACK

8. Yogurt Fruit Parfait

Serves 1 • 5 min

Layers of plain Greek yogurt, diced fruit and rolled oats, topped with chopped nuts and an optional drizzle of honey. It takes five minutes, looks impressive in a glass and is ideal for breakfast buffets, grab-and-go counters and afternoon snack service.

Ingredients

  • 170 g plain Greek yogurt
  • 100 g mixed fresh fruit, diced
  • 20 g rolled oats
  • 10 g unsalted mixed nuts, chopped
  • 1 tsp honey (optional)

Method

  1. Layer yogurt, fruit and oats in a glass.
  2. Top with nuts and optional honey. Serve immediately.

Allergens: Milk, tree nuts, honey

Chef’s note: Assemble close to service so the oats keep some bite. Always declare nuts and offer a nut-free version.

LUNCH

9. Chickpea Spinach Wrap

Serves 1 • 10 min

Mashed chickpeas with yogurt, lemon and cumin, rolled in a whole-wheat tortilla with spinach, cucumber and tomato. The mash holds the filling together like a spread, so the wrap travels well and suits packed lunches and picnic menus.

Ingredients

  • 1 whole-wheat tortilla
  • 100 g cooked chickpeas, drained
  • 30 g spinach
  • ¼ cucumber, diced
  • ½ tomato, diced
  • 2 tbsp plain yogurt
  • 1 tsp lemon juice
  • ¼ tsp ground cumin

Method

  1. Mash chickpeas with yogurt, lemon and cumin.
  2. Spread on tortilla. Add spinach, cucumber and tomato.
  3. Fold in the sides, roll tightly and slice.

Allergens: Wheat (gluten), milk

Chef’s note: Fold the sides in before rolling for a tight wrap. Slice on the diagonal for a cleaner presentation.

LUNCH OR DINNER

10. Sweet Potato & Bean Bowl

Serves 1 • 35 min

Roasted sweet potato cubes with paprika, warm kidney beans and sweetcorn, served over lettuce and tomato and finished with lime juice. The roasting concentrates the natural sweetness, and the beans make the bowl hearty without any meat.

Ingredients

  • 150 g sweet potato, small cubes
  • 100 g cooked kidney beans, drained
  • 50 g sweetcorn
  • ½ tomato, diced
  • 30 g lettuce
  • 1 tsp olive oil
  • 1 tbsp lime juice
  • ¼ tsp paprika

Method

  1. Toss sweet potato with oil and paprika. Roast at 200°C for 25 minutes until tender.
  2. Warm beans and corn. Serve with sweet potato, lettuce and tomato.
  3. Finish with lime juice.

Allergens: None of the major allergens as written

Chef’s note: Cut the cubes evenly so they roast at the same speed. Use properly cooked or canned kidney beans, never undercooked dried ones.

DINNER

11. Mushroom Pea Pasta

Serves 1 • 20 min

Whole-wheat pasta tossed with sautéed mushrooms, garlic, spinach and sweet peas, finished with a little Parmesan and a splash of pasta water. The starchy water creates a light sauce with no cream at all.

Ingredients

  • 60 g dry whole-wheat pasta
  • 100 g mushrooms, sliced
  • 50 g frozen peas
  • 30 g spinach
  • 1 garlic clove, minced
  • 1 tsp olive oil
  • 10 g grated Parmesan
  • Black pepper, to taste

Method

  1. Cook pasta as directed; add peas for the final 3 minutes. Save a little pasta water.
  2. Sauté mushrooms and garlic in oil. Add spinach.
  3. Toss with pasta, peas, Parmesan and a splash of pasta water.

Allergens: Wheat (gluten), milk

Chef’s note: Save the pasta water before draining, because it is the secret to a silky sauce. Brown the mushrooms properly for flavour.

BREAKFAST

12. Apple Cinnamon Overnight Oats

Serves 1 • Chill overnight

Oats, low-fat milk, yogurt, chia and cinnamon soaked in a covered jar overnight and topped with fresh apple and walnuts. There is no cooking, which makes it ideal for grab-and-go breakfast cases and early starts.

Ingredients

  • 40 g rolled oats
  • 100 ml low-fat milk
  • 100 g plain yogurt
  • ½ apple, diced
  • 1 tsp chia seeds
  • ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
  • 10 g walnuts, chopped

Method

  1. Mix oats, milk, yogurt, chia and cinnamon in a covered jar.
  2. Refrigerate overnight.
  3. Top with apple and walnuts before serving.

Allergens: Milk, tree nuts (walnuts), oats (gluten cross-contact)

Chef’s note: Label each jar with the date and keep it refrigerated at all times. Add the apple and walnuts just before service to keep them fresh and crunchy.

DINNER

13. Tofu Vegetable Rice Bowl

Serves 1 • 20 min

Golden pan-fried tofu cubes with broccoli and bell pepper over steaming brown rice, seasoned lightly with reduced-sodium soy sauce. Patting the tofu dry before frying gives a crisp outside and a soft centre.

Ingredients

  • 150 g firm tofu, drained and cubed
  • 150 g cooked brown rice
  • 80 g broccoli, small florets
  • ½ bell pepper, sliced
  • 1 garlic clove, minced
  • 1 tsp olive oil
  • 1 tsp reduced-sodium soy sauce

Method

  1. Pat tofu dry. Pan-fry in oil until golden.
  2. Add garlic, vegetables and a splash of water. Cook until tender.
  3. Stir in soy sauce. Serve over steaming-hot rice.

Allergens: Soy (and usually wheat in soy sauce)

Chef’s note: Do not stir the tofu too early, because it needs time to form a crust. Keep soy dishes clearly labelled.

BREAKFAST OR BRUNCH

14. Tomato Spinach Eggs

Serves 1 • 20 min

Eggs baked in a simmered sauce of tomato, onion, garlic, cumin and spinach, served with a slice of whole-wheat toast. The dish is cooked in one pan and arrives at the table sizzling, which makes it a brunch favourite.

Ingredients

  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g chopped tomatoes
  • 30 g spinach
  • ¼ onion, chopped
  • 1 garlic clove, minced
  • 1 tsp olive oil
  • ¼ tsp ground cumin
  • 1 slice whole-wheat toast

Method

  1. Sauté onion and garlic in oil. Add tomatoes and cumin; simmer 8 minutes.
  2. Stir in spinach. Make two wells and crack in eggs.
  3. Cover and cook until whites and yolks are set. Serve with toast.

Allergens: Egg, wheat (toast)

Chef’s note: Cover the pan so the tops of the eggs cook through, and confirm whites and yolks are set. Serve straight from the pan for the best presentation.

LUNCH

15. Lemon Couscous Chickpeas

Serves 1 • 15 min

Whole-wheat couscous fluffed with boiling water and mixed with chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, parsley, lemon and olive oil. It is served at room temperature, so it works well on buffets and in lunch boxes.

Ingredients

  • 50 g dry whole-wheat couscous
  • 100 g cooked chickpeas, drained
  • ¼ cucumber, diced
  • 1 small tomato, diced
  • 1 tbsp chopped parsley
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • 1 tsp olive oil

Method

  1. Prepare couscous with boiling water as directed on the pack.
  2. Fluff with a fork and cool slightly.
  3. Mix with chickpeas, vegetables, parsley, lemon and oil.

Allergens: Wheat (gluten)

Chef’s note: Fluff with a fork rather than a spoon to keep the grains separate. Keep cold buffet items at safe cold-holding temperatures.

BREAKFAST

16. Banana Oat Pancakes

Serves 1 • 15 min

Small pancakes made by blending ripe banana, egg, oats, milk, baking powder and cinnamon, cooked gently and served with fresh berries. The banana provides all the sweetness, so there is no need for added sugar in the batter.

Ingredients

  • 1 small ripe banana
  • 1 egg
  • 40 g rolled oats
  • 2 tbsp milk
  • ¼ tsp baking powder
  • ¼ tsp cinnamon
  • 1 tsp oil
  • 50 g berries, to serve

Method

  1. Blend banana, egg, oats, milk, baking powder and cinnamon.
  2. Lightly oil a non-stick pan. Cook small pancakes over medium-low heat.
  3. Flip and cook until set through. Serve with berries.

Allergens: Egg, milk, oats (gluten cross-contact)

Chef’s note: Keep the heat medium-low and the pancakes small, since the batter is delicate. Wait for the edges to set before flipping.

Food Safety and Allergens

A healthy dish is only a good dish if it is safe. Raw chicken must be cooked until the centre reaches 74°C, which is why the Chicken Quinoa Bowl and the Chicken Brown Rice Stir-Fry both stress a full cook. Fish is ready when it turns opaque and flakes easily. Eggs should be set through, and the whites and yolks in the Tomato Spinach Eggs should be firm before service.

Cooked rice and other grains need fast cooling and prompt refrigeration, and cold items such as the Yogurt Fruit Parfait, the overnight oats and the couscous salad must stay at safe cold-holding temperatures until the moment they are served. Wash all vegetables and fruit, use separate boards and knives for raw proteins, and keep raw and ready-to-eat foods apart in the fridge. Pulses such as kidney beans must be properly cooked or bought ready-cooked.

Allergens deserve the same discipline. Between them, these recipes contain egg, milk, fish, soy, wheat, tree nuts and oats, and soy sauce normally contains wheat. Oats can also be cross-contaminated with gluten, so a coeliac guest needs certified gluten-free oats. Declare allergens on the menu, brief the service team before every shift and follow your written allergen procedure without exception. If a guest's allergy is uncertain, check with the kitchen rather than guess.

Building a Weekly Menu and Scaling Up

Sixteen recipes can be turned into a simple rotation. For breakfast, alternate the Oatmeal Berry Bowl, Vegetable Omelette, Yogurt Fruit Parfait, Apple Cinnamon Overnight Oats, Tomato Spinach Eggs and Banana Oat Pancakes across the week so that regular guests see variety. For lunch, the Chickpea Avocado Salad, Chickpea Spinach Wrap, Lemon Couscous Chickpeas and Chicken Quinoa Bowl are quick to assemble and travel well. For dinner, the Baked Fish and Vegetables, Chicken Brown Rice Stir-Fry, Mushroom Pea Pasta, Tofu Vegetable Rice Bowl, Sweet Potato and Bean Bowl and Lentil Vegetable Soup give guests a range of proteins, including fully vegetarian and vegan options.

Because every recipe uses a small set of shared ingredients, such as spinach, tomato, cucumber, chickpeas, brown rice and olive oil, buying is simple, waste is low and food cost is predictable. Prep can be shared too: one pan of cooked brown rice serves both the stir-fry and the tofu bowl, and one batch of roasted vegetables can support several plates.

To scale a recipe, multiply each ingredient by the number of portions, but taste and adjust seasoning as you go, because spices and salt do not always scale in a straight line. Weigh the main ingredients for every portion so that plates look the same from one shift to the next and costs stay on target.

Training Your Team

Use these recipes as a short training module. Ask each team member to name the main allergens in three dishes, describe the safe cooking temperature for chicken, explain why pasta water is saved, and identify which recipes are vegan. Then have them cook one recipe from the poster while a supervisor checks weights, timings and presentation. Confident answers and consistent plates turn a recipe card into real service quality.

Final Thoughts

Healthy eating does not have to be dull, expensive or complicated. Sixteen simple meals, built from fresh ingredients, gentle cooking and clear allergen communication, can anchor a menu that guests return to day after day. Start with the recipes that suit your guests best, train the team on the safety points, and use the poster as a quick reference in the kitchen. Fresh ingredients, simple cooking and everyday variety are a strong foundation for any hospitality operation.
